# 2026-10-29 — Release pipeline: dedicated workflow, signed APK, auto-generated notes (issues #5, follow-ups)
- **Context:** Three release problems fixed in sequence: issue #5 asked for the APK on GitHub Releases; the first release (v1.0.0) published an **unsigned** APK that Android rejected with "package appears to be corrupt" (no `META-INF/*.SF|RSA|DSA` block at all); and the release body was a generic one-liner with no information about what changed.
- **Lesson:** (1) Keep release publishing in a separate `release.yml` (tag `v*` push or `workflow_dispatch`) so it stays out of the PR CI path; scope `contents: write` to the release job only. (2) Signing is not optional for distribution — `assembleRelease` without a `signingConfig` can never install on a device. The zero-config approach for a single-user app is an ephemeral keystore generated in CI (`keytool -genkeypair`) + `apksigner sign`/`verify`, with no repository secrets; the trade-off is that each release uses a different key, so later releases can't update in place over earlier ones (fine for a personal app; a stored keystore secret is the fix if that ever matters). (3) Release notes must always be generated: `actions/checkout` needs `fetch-depth: 0` to see tags, notes come from `git log <prev-tag>..HEAD` (merge commits condensed to `(#N) title`) via `gh release create --notes-file`, with an explicit fallback line when the range is empty (re-run of the same tag).
- **Rule now:** `release.yml` builds `assembleRelease`, signs with the ephemeral CI keystore, verifies the signature, and publishes only the signed `app-release.apk` with commit-derived notes. Documented in the `docs/WORKFLOW.md` pipelines table.
